description_full: California Resources Corporation operates as an independent energy and carbon management company in the United States. The company operates in two segments, Oil and Natural Gas, and Carbon Management. It explores, develops, and produces crude oil, oil condensate, natural gas liquids and natural gas to california refineries, marketers, and other purchasers. The company also provides Carbon TerraVault which builds, installs, operates, and maintains CO2 capture equipment, transportation assets, and storage facilities. In addition, it owns and operates power generation facilities, as well as smaller gas-fired power plants used to generate power for oil and natural gas operations. The company was incorporated in 2014 and is based in Long Beach, California.

financial_summary: California Resources Corporatio is a mid-cap energy business with a $4.0B market cap on $3.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +7.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $543M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.38× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.6×.
Management returns a meaningful 12.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.9% of the shares.

Geopolitical supply shocks — wars, sanctions, and OPEC decisions create volatility that no hedging programme can fully neutralise.

Capex runs only 0.6x depreciation (8.8% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
It has missed earnings estimates by 4.2% on average.
Analysts expect -29.0% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.9%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).

It returns 12.8% a year to shareholders (9.4% in buybacks and 3.7% in dividends).
